reuse.why: Collapses five copied provider link functions onto linkProviderAccount/saveLinkedAccount/finishLinkingAccount, the three copied download functions onto downloadProviderTransactions, reuses link.findOrCreateBank, and makes unlinkAccount and the takeover share releaseAccountLinks.

duplication.why: Removes most of the existing per-provider copies; linkGoCardlessAccount still spells out the assert/findOrCreateBank/release/save/sync/finish sequence that linkProviderAccount owns.

placement.why: Link rules and provider wiring stay in accounts/app.ts, sync.ts and server-config.ts where the tree keeps them; the link-check could arguably live in link.ts next to findOrCreateBank.

scope.why: Focused on linking and Fintegra sync; the two desktop-client map entries are forced by the provider type list, and the refactor of existing providers is broad but in service of the steps.

maintainability.why: A new provider is now a few lines and the link rules are in one guard; nits are that assertBankAccountNotLinked both asserts and returns ids to release, and getAccountToUpgrade is fetched twice per upgrade.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All providers, GoCardless included, go through assertBankAccountNotLinked, releaseAccountLinks, saveLinkedAccount and finishLinkingAccount; unlinkAccount reuses releaseAccountLinks.

disguised_duplication.where: The remaining GoCardless orchestration is a visible sequence of calls to the shared helpers, not a reshaped copy of their logic.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked gains replaceExistingLink and the closed-account branch; linkProviderAccount takes fileId (Pluggy) and tables (Akahu's preserved ['transactions']); linkGoCardlessAccount keeps its own orchestration instead of linkProviderAccount because its account shape differs.
